meta.face: An Egyptian of about seventy-five, sun-browned to a deep bronze, with a WIDE, LOW, ROUNDED-SQUARE face, broad through the jaw — a short, lined forehead half hidden by the hood, a short, broad nose with a rounded tip, narrow dark eyes deeply creased at the corners by a quiet smile, thick, low grey brows, broad cheeks lifted by the smile, a wide, kindly mouth; only a thin, short, sparse grey beard and moustache; the gaze warm and a little amused, toward us.
meta.basis: The Painter's Manual gives Macarius of Alexandria a single mark, a smiling face, which the card makes its keynote; the Blaj iconostasis icon (Wikipedia lead image) gives the dark hood and a short, thin beard. The book supplies the attributes: the basket of sand he carried to tame himself and the grapes he passed on untasted. Wikipedia (born c. 300, died 395) gives his old age. Kept apart from `anthony_abbot` (triangular, long beard) and `francis_paola` (square, long white beard) by the wide smiling face and sparse beard.
